provenance.l: Apollo 12 Mission Report MSC-01855 (Mar 1970): Table 5-IX, entry interface 244:22:19.1 at 400,000 ft, 36,116 ft/s (11,009 m/s), flight-path angle -6.48 deg; Table A-II, command module weight at entry 12,275.5 lb (5,568 kg; the OCR of this row is doubtful); section 11.3.1, landing 244:36:25 GET (20:58:25 GMT 24 November 1969) at 15 deg 46.6 min S, 165 deg 9.0 min W, USS Hornet. Quote: "The command module landed at 244:36:25 (2058 G.m.t.) at a point calculated by recovery forces to be 15 degrees 46.6 minutes south latitude and 165 degrees 9.0 minutes west longitude." Impact: "the landing impact was extremely hard ... an impact acceleration of about 15g" (section 9.15); the model has no water-impact load, so this is a description, not a fitted value. Flotation (B1): Apollo 12 Mission Report MSC-01855 section 11.3.1, flotation: the command module "immediately went to the stable II (apex down) attitude. The uprighting system returned the command module to the stable I attitude 4 minutes 26 seconds later." Drawn on screen sooner (afterTouchdown beats); realAfterS 266 s

NASA SP-4029 Apollo chronology, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" compilation (Apollo 7-17): entry interface velocity, flight-path angle, lift-to-drag ratio, range to target, maximum g, entry-to-splashdown duration, splashdown position and CM weight. Apollo 12 column: "Lift To Drag Ratio 0.309", "Range (n mi) 1,250" (1,250 n.mi = 2,315 km), "Maximum g 6.57", "Duration (sec) 845.9", "Velocity (ft/sec) 36,116.618", "Flight Path Angle -6.48". No Apollo 12 entry postflight analysis was found, so L/D and range are the compilation values (secondary), not a reconstruction; there is no published first/second load-factor split. Model limit: with these inputs the model peaks at 7.6 g at 68 s (6.57 g flown), dips to 1.1 g, second pulse 5.9 g; drogues 486 s (504 s flown, 8 min 24 s), splashdown 840 s (846 s flown)
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
